description: Official async Rust client for the Checkslip API: look up a Thai bank transfer with the sending bank from the QR code on a slip or from a photo of it. Minimum supported Rust version 1.75.
rules: Add the crate with cargo add checkslip. Webhook signature checking is behind the webhooks feature.
Build the client with Client::builder().api_key(key).build()?, then reach groups through accessors such as client.slips() and client.billing().
Look up a slip with slips().lookup(LookupRequest::qr(qr)) or LookupRequest::image(bytes).
Lists come in pairs: list() returns one page, list_all() returns a stream over every page.
Read the API key from the environment and keep it on a server. Never hard-code it and never ship it to a browser.
Checkslip looks up the transfer with the sending bank and returns what the bank holds. It does not judge whether a slip is real or fake; accepting the payment is the caller's decision.
Amounts come back in satang, where 100 satang is 1 baht. Account numbers come back as the last four digits only.
FOUND, NOT_FOUND and DUPLICATE are normal outcomes and are returned, not raised. Only a problem with the request itself is an error.
A lookup is answered in one call: the lookup endpoint does not answer with 202 and does not return the PENDING outcome, and when the bank does not show the transfer you get a 503 UNAVAILABLE error.
Pass your own idempotency key when a job can be retried across processes, so a repeat returns the first answer and is never charged twice.
Check the signature of every webhook before trusting it, and pass both secrets during a rotation.
